# TRI — Portfolio Construction Recommendation
**Thomson Reuters Corp. | $117.23 (verified feed) | Mkt cap $52.7bn | EV $54.2bn**
*Synthesis of 12 specialist reports; four conflicted metrics independently re-verified.*

---

## 0. Data Reconciliation (before sizing)

The specialist reports disagreed materially on four inputs. My verified readings take precedence:

| Metric | Verified value | Conflict resolved |
|---|---|---|
| Price / mkt cap | **$117.23 / $52.70bn** | Matches consensus; some agents used $50.8bn (stale share count) |
| P/E (GAAP TTM) | **34.5x**; P/B 4.42x; EV/EBITDA **17.8x**; P/FCF **25.7x** | Value Researcher's 27.6x is *forward adjusted* — both are correct, different denominators. Use GAAP when comparing to growth; adjusted for peer work |
| FCF yield | **3.89%** (on $2.05bn FCF) | Fin Risk's 4.14% and Value's 4.5% used inflated FCF or stale cap. **3.9% is the number.** Div yield 2.9% |
| Volatility | **46.0% ann.** (504d), max DD **−63.5%**, Sharpe **−0.49** | Settles the 39.7% vs 57.7% dispute. Beta 0.13 is **not usable** (R²≈0) — the benchmark join is broken, corroborated by SPY correlations of 0.003–0.13 across *all* five names |
| Correlation | TRI–RELX **0.70**, TRI–VRSK **0.69**, TRI–SPGI **0.57**, TRI–MSCI 0.48 | Cross-sectional correlations are usable even though SPY link is broken. **This is the key portfolio fact** (see §4) |
| Street targets | 8 recent: 85, 87, 110, 130, 130, 135, 138, 183 → **median $130** | Confirms extreme dispersion ($85–183) and a still-declining trend (UBS $215→$183, Barclays $210→$130, MS $116→$110) |

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sector Researcher** | Constructive / Sector ATTRACTIVE | **Medium-High** | Highest gross margin in true comp set (75.8%, +11pp vs median) but **only large cap with −7.7pp operating-margin trajectory**; 2026 organic re-accel (8.5–9.0%) puts it above peer median for first time since 2022. Preference within sector is for *margin-expanding* ARPU monetisers (RELX/SPGI/VRSK) — TRI is on the wrong side until margin inflects |
| **Geo Legal** | Positive / Risk LOW | **High** | Revenue 88% recurring, USD, developed-market, no sanctions exposure. Third Circuit ROSS win (29 Sep 26) *monetises* the content moat. E-invoicing mandates are a demand tailwind. Only escalation path: TRI as AI-copyright *defendant*, or CLEAR privacy action |
| **Macro** | Neutral, **negative skew** | **Medium-High** | Business fine, valuation regime hostile: 10Y real yield +65bp to 2.69%, Fed back to hiking (3.88%), market pricing +85bp. ~30x long-duration multiple is the transmission channel — −22.8% over 12m *while* organic accelerated. Bear case $85–95 on unchanged EPS |
| **Value Researcher** | **HOLD** — accumulate <$95–100 | **High** | Moat WIDE (ROIC 14–16% vs WACC 7.5–8%), IV ≈ **$135** (range $124–145), bear $78 / bull $160. At $117 = **87% of IV — no margin of safety**. 25% MoS requires ~$101. FCF flat 4 years ($2.26bn 2021 → $2.05bn 2025) on +18% revenue |
| **Growth Researcher** | **BUY** (not Strong Buy) | **High** | 10% organic, Big 3 +10% for two consecutive quarters, transactions +23%, gen-AI = 34% of ACV. FV **$135–150** on 18–19x 2027E EBITDA. Admits Rule of 40 only ~34, 2026 adj. EPS +3%, and disruption *deferred not resolved* |
| **Fin Risk Analyst** | **MODERATE** (solvency-safe, equity-fragile) | **High** | Credit A−/0.77x net leverage/11.7x coverage — non-issue. Survives −30% revenue at 1.57x. **But**: 46–58% vol, −63.5% DD, and debt +$1.69bn in 9 months while buying back stock at $200+ (shareholder returns 124% of FCF) = **credible capital-allocation error** |
| **Non-Fin Risk Analyst** | **HIGH** | **High** | C-Track breach (access Mar → detect 30 Jun → disclose 2 Sep, sealed court records, 12+ US states + Canada); **repeat** privacy pattern ($27.5M CA 2025 → MI class action May 26 → C-Track); new CFO in a complex capital-markets year; ~C$74M insider selling / zero open-market buying; ~70% Woodbridge control |
| **Quant Analyst** | **SELL** (composite 28/100) | **Medium** (self-flags corrupted inputs) | Value 22, Momentum 18, Low-Vol **6** (2nd percentile), Revisions 33. TTM −18%, 12-1 ≈ −27%, −43.7% from Jul-25 peak. Offsetting: +45% off Feb trough, accruals −6.7%, F=7. "Broken-momentum de-rating, not balance-sheet failure" |
| **Short Analyst** | **NO EDGE** — reject short; "no long either" | **High** (forensic) | Beneish **−2.79**, accruals −6.7%, OCF/NI 1.80x, AR *falling* vs rising revenue, gross margin stable at 75.8%. **Not a fraud.** But flags the one real numeric divergence: reported revenue +2.9% (Q3) vs "Big 3 organic +10%" — a ~600bp wedge; and capex/D&A 0.69x flatters FCF by ~14% |

But "beats unrewarded, misses punished" regime; resolves on the margin line 4 Feb 2027 |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **MEDIUM-LOW — constructive on the business, split on the price**

**Genuine consensus (high agreement, high weight):**
1. **The moat is real and it is not a fraud.** Value (WIDE moat, ROIC 14–16%), Short (Beneish −2.79, 180% cash conversion), Sector (highest gross margin in comp set), Non-Fin (ROSS win) all converge. Gross margin has held at 75–77% through the entire AI panic — the strongest single refutation of the bear case.
2. **The balance sheet is not the risk; terminal value is.** Fin Risk, Short, Value agree. Credit was *upgraded* into the equity collapse.
3. **AI disruption is a 2027–2030 terminal-value question, not a 2026 earnings question.** Sector, Short, Growth, Alt Data all say churn moves at contract-renewal pace.
4. **Operating margin is the swing variable.** Sector (−7.7pp), Growth (46.6% vs 49.0% Legal EBITDA margin), Fin Risk (op. income −32% on +2.9% revenue), Alt Data, Macro all independently nominate the same metric. **This is the position's single KPI.**

**Contested (weight in the sizing decision):**
- *Price*: Growth says BUY at 17.8x EV/EBITDA; Value says HOLD until $101. Both are internally consistent — Growth capitalises a 2027 recovery, Value refuses to pay for it. I weight Value higher on **entry discipline** and Growth higher on **direction**.
- *Momentum*: Quant says SELL; Short says the bear case is "already half-paid-out" after −62% peak-to-trough. Quant's own inputs are partially corrupted and its Sharpe (+1.06) is a window artifact. I discount Quant to a *timing* signal, not a thesis signal.

**Conflict resolution (per framework: the risk flag governs):** Non-Fin's HIGH rating and Fin Risk's capital-allocation finding take precedence over Growth's BUY and Value's HOLD-for-quality. A business with a repeat data-breach pattern and management buying back stock at $200 with borrowed money does **not** earn a full-size position, however good the franchise. → **Reduced size, staged entry.**

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **1.5% of portfolio (target), 0.5% initiated now**

| Input | Reading | Sizing effect |
|---|---|---|
| Conviction | Medium (split) | Caps at the 1–3% band |
| Multiple risk flags | Non-Fin **HIGH**, Quant **SELL**, Macro negative skew | Drives to the **low end** of that band |
| Total volatility | **46%** — 3x a typical 15% portfolio name | A 1.5% position contributes ~0.69% standalone portfolio vol; **acceptable** but no larger |
| Edge / odds | Base IV $135 vs $117 = +15%; bear $78–95 = −19% to −33%; probability-weighted (25/50/25) ≈ $127 = **+8%** | Kelly: edge is thin. f* ≈ edge/odds ≈ 0.08/0.35 ≈ 23% of a *fully-convicted* allocation. **Confirms small size.** |
| Correlation to likely existing holdings | 0.70 to RELX, 0.69 to VRSK, 0.57 to SPGI | If RELX/VRSK/SPGI are already owned, **cap the aggregate info-services sleeve** (§4) |

**Verdict: 1.5% target — a "toe-hold plus optionality" position, not a core holding.** Explicitly, this is sized by **total volatility, not beta**: 0.13 beta would imply a 5%+ position and would be a serious error, since the −63.5% drawdown was almost entirely idiosyncratic and beta-hedging would have offered no protection.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Sector.** GICS files TRI under *Industrials / Specialty Business Services* — a misclassification that will make any sector-exposure report understate information-services concentration. Economically it belongs with RELX/VRSK/SPGI/MSCI/FDS/WKL. **Test before adding: if the book already owns RELX or VRSK, TRI is a fourth bet on the same AI-terminal-value question, at 0.69–0.70 correlation.** At that correlation, 1.5% TRI plus 3% RELX plus 2% VRSK is one ~4% factor bet, not three diversifiers. **Hard cap: aggregate information-services exposure (TRI + RELX + VRSK + SPGI + MSCI + FDS) ≤ 8% of portfolio.**

**Factor exposure — net negative additions on three axes:**
- **Momentum:** adds a 12-1 ≈ −27%, 2nd-percentile name. If the book has a momentum or quality-momentum tilt, this is an active anti-momentum bet. Acceptable only as a deliberate value/contrarian sleeve.
- **Duration:** long-duration, real-rate-sensitive. At 2.69% real 10Y and a hiking Fed, **do not fund this from cash while also holding other 25x+ long-duration compounders** — that is a doubled bet on term premium.
- **Low-vol / defensive:** the label is a trap. Beta 0.13, but 46% realized vol and a −63.5% drawdown. **This will not behave defensively in a growth scare** despite the beta suggesting it will.
- **Offsetting positive:** near-zero correlation to broad equity (idiosyncratic), so it *does* diversify market beta at the portfolio level even though it is volatile standalone. That is the whole case for holding 1.5% rather than 0%.

**Correlation.** Primary risk is intra-sleeve, not vs. SPY.

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale in, 40/30/30 — do not buy at once**

At $117.23 the stock is at **87% of base intrinsic value ($135)** — a 13% discount, not a margin of safety. Value's 25%-MoS entry is ~$101. The Feb 4 2027 print is a genuine binary on the *one* metric that matters (margin), and Q3 already missed EPS by 9%.

| Tranche | Size | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **T1 — now** | **0.5%** | Establish the position. Demand alt-data (traffic +11.9% MoM, FDE hiring, 34% AI share of ACV) is genuinely green and the stock is 43% off its peak. Own some. |
| **T2 — 0.5%** | on **price ≤ $103–105** (near Value's $101 MoS threshold) **OR** post-Q4 confirmation of organic ≥8.5% with adjusted EBITDA margin ≥39.0% | Whichever comes first. Do not chase strength. |
| **T3 — 0.5%** | **only** on demonstrated **operating-margin inflection** — either Legal Professionals adj. EBITDA margin recovering above 49%, or group operating margin expanding 100bp+ y/y, or a marquee Thomson LLM licensing deal | This tranche is paid for by proof, not by narrative. If margin never inflects, T3 is never funded and the final position is 1.0%. |

**Do not** use the current 34.5x GAAP / 17.8x EV-EBITDA as evidence of cheapness. Using the verified 3.9% FCF yield and flat four-year FCF, the market is capitalising ~4–5% perpetual FCF growth — mildly pessimistic, not absurd.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Stop-loss discipline — price *and* fundamental, with the fundamental dominant.** At 46% annualised vol, a mechanical 15% stop is ~5 weeks of ordinary noise and would almost certainly be triggered by nothing. Therefore:

- **Hard review trigger: $90** (−23%, near the Feb-2026 $78.53 low zone). At $90 the stock is ~2/3 of base IV and inside Value's bear-case band ($78–95). *Trigger a full re-underwrite, not an automatic exit* — the bear case may already be in the price. Cut to 0.5% if the review finds any fundamental trigger also hit.
- **Position size is the primary risk control**, not the stop. 1.5% × −33% bear case = **−50bp of portfolio** — a loss the book absorbs without a decision. That is the design.

**Thesis invalidation (any one → exit fully, regardless of price):**
1. **Organic revenue growth <6% for two consecutive quarters** (from 8.5–9.0% guided). Value, Short, Growth and Sector all independently nominate this.
2. **Gross margin breaks below 74%** (currently 75.8%; four-year range 75.3–77.0%). Short Analyst's designated short trigger. This is the earliest hard evidence that AI is eroding Westlaw pricing.
3. **Disclosed net revenue retention deterioration, or explicit seat-count/ARR decline** in Legal Professionals.
4. **A goodwill impairment charge** (goodwill + intangibles = 112% of equity; tangible book −$1.3bn) — the bear case's actual transmission mechanism.
5. **A state AG enforcement action or injunction against CLEAR/PeopleMap data sourcing**, or confirmation the C-Track breach exposed sealed records at scale. Non-Fin's escalation item #2 (repeat privacy failure) is the one governance flag I will not tolerate through a second cycle.
6. **The revenue-reconciliation gap the Short Analyst flagged** — if the ~600bp wedge between reported total growth and "Big 3 organic +10%" turns out to be a promotional organic definition, thesis is void.

**Trim trigger:**
- **$135 (base intrinsic value) → trim one-third.** Rule: never let a 1.5% position become a 3% position on re-rating; that converts a value trade into an accidental momentum bet.
- **$145–150 (upper IV / Growth's bull case) → reduce to 0.5%.** The franchise is priced for success; recycle into names still on the wrong side of the margin trade per the Sector Researcher's preference ranking (RELX, SPGI, VRSK).
- **Trim 0.25% into the Feb 4 print** if the position is at full 1.5% and the stock is above $125 — the outcome distribution around that EPS line is genuinely wide.

**Monitoring calendar:** Feb 4 2027 (Q4/FY26 + first FY27 guide — the decisive event); quarterly operating margin and Legal segment EBITDA margin; any AI-copyright suit naming TRI as defendant.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE — 0.5% starter, 1.5% target**

**Rationale in one paragraph.** Eleven of twelve agents agree this is a wide-moat, cash-generative, A−-rated franchise whose gross margin has held at 76% straight through the most violent AI-disruption repricing in the sector's history; the forensic work is unambiguous that there is no accounting problem. That gets it on the book. But the agents also converge — from five independent directions — that the **operating margin is compressing** (−7.7pp, Legal EBITDA margin 46.6% vs 49.0%, Q3 op. income −32% on +2.9% revenue), and no one has yet shown that AI is accretive to margin rather than merely to revenue. At 34.5x GAAP earnings, a 3.9% FCF yield, four years of flat FCF, 46% volatility, a HIGH non-financial risk rating from a repeat data-breach pattern, and management that repurchased stock at $200 with borrowed money, this is a **fairly-priced quality business with a contested terminal value — not a margin-of-safety opportunity.** The honest answer is not Buy or Pass; it is **own a small amount, get paid 2.9% to wait, and let the margin line in February decide whether it becomes a 1.5% position or a 0.5% one.**

**Cross-agent dissent on the record:** Growth would take the full 3%. Value would take none until $101. I am deliberately between them, closer to Value on entry price and closer to Growth on direction — and I over-weight Non-Fin and Fin Risk relative to their nominal domain, because on a position whose entire debate is terminal value, the governance and capital-allocation record *is* the terminal value.

## SECTOR BRIEF — Thomson Reuters (TRI)

**Classification note:** FMP files TRI under *Industrials / Specialty Business Services*, alongside 27% of the S&P Industrials by cap (SpaceX, GE, CAT, RTX). That aggregate (21 companies, FY25 revenue $797bn, **31.8% gross margin**) is an economically meaningless benchmark for a 76%-gross-margin subscription information business. I have therefore benchmarked TRI against its true competitive set — information services & analytics (RELX, SPGI, MSCI, VRSK, FDS, MORN, CLVT) — and flagged where data was unavailable.

---

### 1. Sector Overview

TRI competes in **professional information services & decision-support analytics** — legal research, tax & accounting workflow, regulatory/compliance content — a roughly $60–80bn global pool growing mid-to-high single digits, of which legal AI is only ~$3.3bn in 2026 (Precedence Research) but compounding at 20%+. Structurally it is a **duopoly-plus oligopoly**: legal research is effectively TRI versus LexisNexis (RELX), which together hold an estimated 70–80% share (HHI est. ~2,500–3,000, highly concentrated), with vLex/Fastcase and Wolters Kluwer at the fringe. Barriers are high on proprietary content, citation/verification trust, and workflow embedding (multi-year subscriptions, high switching costs), but 2024–26 has introduced a **new and dangerous entry vector**: AI-native platforms (Harvey ~$190m ARR at end-2025, Legora, Luminance, Robin AI) that bypass the content-licensing moat by orchestrating foundation models. The sector is **mature/late-cycle in its core research business but in early-stage re-acceleration** as generative AI adds ARPU and regulation (e-invoicing) forces non-discretionary spend — a barbell between a defensive base and a highly contested growth layer.

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Regulation as a demand engine (non-discretionary).** E-invoicing is now active policy in **60+ markets** with mandates phasing through 2026–27 (EU ViDA, Germany, France, Poland, Malaysia), pulling compliance and reporting spend forward. This directly feeds TRI's Corporates and Tax/Audit/Accounting segments and is largely immune to macro conditions — the classic reason these models carry beta of ~0.17.
- **Gen-AI monetisation is now measurable, not speculative.** Generative AI products reached **34% of annualised contract value** in Q3-26, with total organic revenue +10% and the "Big 3" segments +10% organic for a **second consecutive quarter** — evidence of genuine ARPU uplift rather than cannibalisation so far.
- **Portfolio simplification toward higher-quality revenue.** The 51% Global Print sale to KKR (~$500m, closed 1 Oct 2026) exits structurally declining, low-margin print, **adding 60–70bps to organic growth from Q4-26** and lifting group margin. Combined with a completed $600m buyback and $2.0bn debt raise, capital allocation now skews to AI/content M&A.

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Foundation-model supplier power is the central structural risk.** OpenAI/Anthropic/Google are simultaneously partners and potential captors of the value chain. The cost of serving AI shows up immediately in margins: TRI's D&A rose from $725m (2023) to $930m (2025), and its **operating margin has fallen 770bps** (34.3% → 26.6%) while revenue grew only 10%.
- **AI-native entrants attack the seat-based pricing model.** Harvey's token consumption went from ~1tn to 12tn per month in a few months (July 2026); LexisNexis+ Protégé, vLex/Vincent and Legora are all viable. If AI compresses billable research hours and seats, the incumbent revenue model — not just market share — is at risk.
- **Fading pricing power/FX in the reported numbers.** FY25 reported growth was just **3.0%** (vs 6.8% in FY24) against mid-single-digit organic, i.e. FX/net divestiture drag, and Q3-26 still missed consensus EPS ($0.81 vs $0.89), driving a **9.9% single-day drawdown** — the market is no longer paying indiscriminately for the franchise.

### 4. Peer Comparison Table

Latest reported fiscal year, USD millions.

## 1. Macro Environment Summary

**Stance: Transitional — "late-cycle reflation colliding with a term-premium shock."** This is not a classic risk-on or risk-off tape; it is a regime where earnings are fine and discount rates are hostile.

The defining feature of the last six months is that **long-end yields have risen for the wrong reason**. The US 10Y went from 4.44% (30 Jun 2026) to a peak of 5.31% (5 Oct 2026) and sits at 4.95% (3 Nov 2026) — but 10Y breakevens *fell* over the same window, from 2.40% (late May) to **2.26%** (4 Nov 2026). Inflation expectations are anchored and drifting down; therefore essentially the entire rise is **real yields and term premium** (10Y real ≈ 4.95 − 2.26 = **2.69%**, versus ~2.04% at end-June, +65bp in four months). The 30Y at 5.47% points to fiscal supply/term-premium stress, not growth optimism.

Meanwhile the Fed has **pivoted back to tightening**: after cutting the funds rate from 4.33% (Jan 2025) to 3.63% (May–Aug 2026), the effective rate rose to 3.75% (Sep) and **3.88% (Oct 2026)**. With the 2Y at 4.74% versus an effective 3.88%, the market is pricing roughly **+85bp of further hikes over two years**. So the forward curve is *not* the friend of long-duration equities.

Mitigants: the curve is positively sloped (2s10s **+39bp**, no inversion, no recession signal), unemployment is a low and stable 4.2%, real GDP growth re-accelerated to ~3.4% annualised in Q3 2026, and credit is wide open (HY OAS **3.40%**, ~1pp tighter than a year ago despite widening ~40bp off the September low of 2.66%). This is a "high nominal growth, high real rates, tight credit" world — earnings-supportive, multiple-hostile.

**What would move it to Positive:** credible ESRS-grade disclosure, retirement of offsets in favour of real abatement with an AI-compute Scope 3 target, and a human-rights/data-use review with board-level accountability for the law-enforcement portfolio.

**Bottom line for the memo:** own TRI for AI-driven Legal/Tax compounding and the content moat — *not* for ESG. The ESG work here is a monitoring checklist, not a valuation input.
